A 53-year-old woman presents with a fever 4 days after being discharged following induction
chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). She has no specific symptoms aside from the fever
and has no history of chronic medical conditions other than AML. Her vital signs include a temperature
of 38.8°C (101.8°F), blood pressure of 126/76 mm Hg, heart rate of 82/min, and respiratory rate of
20/min. Physical examination, including the central venous catheter site, skin, head and neck, heart,
lungs, abdomen, and perirectal area, reveals no abnormalities. Laboratory results are as follows: |
Hemoglobin | 9.0 g/dL | | --- | --- | | Leukocyte count | 800/mm3 | | Percent segmented neutrophils | 40%
| | Platelet count | 85,000/mm3 | What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) IV imipenem (B) Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole plus clindamycin (C) IV
piperacillin-tazobactam (D) IV ceftriaxone (E) IV cefepime (F) IV meropenem (G) IV vancomycin (H)
Oral azithromycin plus cefuroxime (I) Oral levofloxacin (J) Oral ciprofloxacin plus amoxicillin-clavulanic
acid
 A. IV imipenem
